label: Branch Piping
iwEaNote: third IW-family value, distinct from IW-A and IW-P, added specifically for this file. Per the CSV's own fbs_function_id_needed field: 'third IW class -- evidence the Func taxonomy gap is real'. Not an EA-* value despite tying into an EA-ST/EA-SB connector at its far end -- the branch itself is IW: it is teed off the header (a pipe-side origin), unlike GD-ST/GD-SB which are wholly external structures.

artifactType.reason: SETTLED 1Sep26 by project decision: SUB-ASSEMBLY, replacing the previous 'Part, open -- not yet formally assessed' state carried from the FBS/OAM reconciliation CSV. GD-B owns a real declared junction (the Tee, verified live) and a real external tie at its far end to a GD-ST/GD-SB connector slot, and is subordinate to the ILS rather than standing alone. Note this is a change of substance, not just of label: the CSV's own reading was Part ('structurally, chain/branch like GD-VLV'), and GD-VLV has now been settled the other way, as a Part. The distinguishing fact is that GD-B's far end ties to a SEPARATE component, whereas GD-VLV's stem terminates free -- an external tie, not an internal sub-member. Sub-Assembly is EDES's own value; see edes:shared#/oam/partAssemblyRule.subAssemblyNote.

note: subclasses component_spec.Component directly, same as edes:GD-VLV -- NOT ExternalStructure, despite tying into one at its far end. GD-B owns real pipe (a Section throughout its own structural lines, per Table XII figures), which neither GD-ST nor GD-SB has; it is closer in kind to GD-VLV's stem (a branch off a main line, terminating in space) than to the EA-ST/EA-SB family, except that GD-VLV's stem terminates free while GD-B's terminates at a real external connector.

edges.note: Func9 is a ProposedFunction, not yet in the authored edes:shared.nodes set -- the third IW-class Function the CSV itself flags as evidence of a real taxonomy gap

same OAM pattern per the CSV: a branch off a main structural line via a declared junction. GD-VLV's stem junction (:smid) and GD-B's Tee junction are both entries returned by the base Component.junctions() method -- GD-B is not introducing a new mechanism, it is the fourth component in this corpus to use one already defined on the base class (the others being GD-PIP's outer-pipe root and GD-VLV's stem root).

GD-B's far end ties to a GD-ST connector slot via top_structure_for_branch(), verified live to produce real node coincidence: for an L-branch (connector_axis='horizontal'), GD-ST's right_connector_y is set to the branch end's y; for a Z-branch (connector_axis='vertical'), GD-ST's top_connector_x is set to the branch end's x. Default GD-ST geometry otherwise, so a branch is always presented on a workable structure. This is a cross-component BUILDER function, not a property either component carries on itself -- GD-B does not know about GD-ST, and GD-ST does not know about GD-B; top_structure_for_branch() is what connects them.

designCode.status: OPEN -- does not fit edes:shared.designCode rule as stated, though closer to fitting than any EA-* component
designCode.reason: shared.designCode's rule realises Func1/Func3 for a pipe-shaped, constant-bore component with no non-pipe interface. GD-B IS pipe-shaped throughout its own structural lines (a real Section, OD_branch/t_branch, Table XII) -- closer to the rule's premise than GD-ST/GD-SB/GD-SH, none of which have a section at all. But GD-B realises neither Func1 (it is not a stand-in on the HEADER's own line) nor Func3 (its wall is not the header's design wall) -- it is a second, independent line that merely originates on the header via a Tee.
designCode.consequence: not evaluated against the rule's actual test (section_at) because that test is about the HEADER at a given x, and GD-B's own section_at(x) always returns None for that reason (see scope.neverOwnsHeaderSection) -- the rule's premise is answered 'no' immediately, without needing to reach the pipe-shaped/non-pipe-interface distinction it was written to make. GD-B's own piping would likely be DNV-governed like the header, but this is not stated in source and is recorded as a gap.

scope.twoVariants: L (3-segment: tee->elbow->valve->end, HORIZONTAL connector axis, sliding guide) and Z (4-segment: tee->elbow1->valve->elbow2->end, VERTICAL connector axis, rigid to the EA-ST top plate) -- Table II / Fig 15. Both verified live: L produces 4 geometry nodes/3 lines, Z produces 5 nodes/4 lines.
scope.neverOwnsHeaderSection: section_at(x) is unconditionally None -- 'teed off; adds no section to the header itself' per source. Verified live. owns(x) is also unconditionally False -- 'teed off the header; owns no span of it' -- distinct from section_at returning None but making the same point from the assembly-ownership-arbitration side rather than the section-query side.
scope.neverOwnsContact: contact_at(x) is unconditionally None and every geometry_line reports owns_contact=False -- 'the branch rises AWAY from the rollers and can never be touched by one', per source and confirmed by the CSV's own contact_ownership field ('none -- excluded by design'). Verified live across both variants, all 3 (L) / 4 (Z) segments.
scope.valveNodeIsMandatoryNotPreferred: the Tee and the valve are BOTH NodePriority.MANDATORY; every other node (elbow(s), end) is PREFERRED. The Tee's reason is standard (a shared structural node either exists or the two lines are not connected -- a beam line cannot attach to the interior of an element). The valve's reason is NOT the standard contact-distribution argument used elsewhere in this corpus (a lumped mass CAN normally be distributed to bracketing nodes by shape functions, same as contact): it fails specifically because this component's OWN mesh_advice sets min_elements=1, so on a single-element horizontal run the bracketing nodes ARE the elbow(s) and the end -- a PREFERRED valve node would let the mesher silently put the 3 mT mass back onto an elbow, exactly the placement P_bv exists to prevent. This was a real, since-fixed defect (see source comment): point_masses() previously returned the elbow node directly while its own docstring claimed mid-run, off by half the run in one direction or the other depending on variant.
scope.p_b3AndP_bcUndocumented: per the CSV's own notes_open_questions field: P_bc (Tee -> nearest EA-ST connection) and P_b3 (Z-variant run elevation) are BOTH undocumented in the source paper. P_b3 is given a placeholder default (P_b2/2, half the total rise) flagged explicitly in source as NOT SPECIFIED IN THE PAPER -- Fig 24 shows the Z's horizontal run at an intermediate height but gives no parameter for it. P_bc, notably, is defined and defaulted (2.5D for L, 1.25D for L... wait -- see params.free note on P_bc's own default_for asymmetry) but is NEVER READ by any geometry, structural, or connector method in the class -- verified by search: no reference to self.P_bc anywhere outside its own field declaration and default_for. It is a stored, validated-by-nothing, displayed-but-unused parameter.
scope.P_bvFixedDefect: point_masses() previously returned the ELBOW node ('elbow' for L, 'elbow2' for Z) despite its own docstring claiming mid-run placement -- at the L default the valve mass sat at x=0.000 and at the Z default at x=4.064, against a true mid-run of 2.032 m, a full half-run error in the moment arm for a 3 mT mass on a cantilevered branch. Fixed by introducing P_bv as a real Optional parameter, resolved in __post_init__ before validate() runs (same ordering fix as edes:GD-ST/edes:GD-SB's P_c1/P_c2). Recorded here as a FIXED defect, not an open one -- see defects.

free.name: variant
free.meaning: BRANCH SHAPE. 'L' turns once and ends horizontally; 'Z' turns twice and ends vertically. A string, not a number.
free.note: 'L' or 'Z' only, validated against VALID_BRANCH_VARIANTS={'L','Z'}. Confirmed live: any other string is rejected.

free.name: P_b1
free.meaning: AXIAL LENGTH of the horizontal run, from the Tee outward.
free.note: horizontal run length. Same default ratio for both variants.

free.name: P_b2
free.meaning: TOTAL VERTICAL RISE from the Tee to the far-end connector.
free.note: TOTAL vertical rise, Tee to connector -- differs by variant per default_for(pipe, variant), verified live (0.8128 m for L, 1.4224 m for Z at STD_PIPELINE).

free.name: P_bc
free.meaning: AXIAL DISTANCE from the Tee to the nearest structure connection point. NOTE: stored and defaulted but READ BY NOTHING -- it drives no geometry.
free.note: Tee -> nearest EA-ST connection point. STORED AND DEFAULTED BUT NEVER READ by any method on this class -- see scope.p_b3AndP_bcUndocumented. Confirmed by source search: appears only in its own field declaration and default_for().

free.name: P_b3
free.meaning: ELEVATION of the Z-variant's horizontal run above the Tee. Z ONLY. Placeholder default with no basis in the source paper.
free.note: elevation of the Z-variant's horizontal run. NOT GIVEN IN THE SOURCE PAPER -- Fig 24 shows an intermediate height with no parameter for it; the half-total-rise default is an explicit placeholder, flagged rather than hidden. Resolved in __post_init__, before validate() checks it strictly between 0 and P_b2.

free.name: P_bv
free.meaning: POSITION OF THE VALVE along the horizontal run, measured from its start elbow. Placeholder default (mid-run) with no basis in the source paper.
free.note: valve position measured along the horizontal run from its start elbow. NOT GIVEN IN THE SOURCE PAPER either -- same treatment as P_b3. Fixed a real defect (see scope.P_bvFixedDefect and defects GD-B-D1). validate() checks it STRICTLY between 0 and P_b1 -- confirmed live at both boundaries (0.0 and P_b1 both rejected) -- because a valve node at either boundary would coincide with an elbow node, giving `path` two entries at one coordinate and a zero-length element.

free.name: OD_branch
free.meaning: OUTSIDE DIAMETER of the branch pipe. Must be smaller than the header's.
free.note: Table XII. Must be strictly less than the header's OD_pipe -- confirmed live.

free.name: t_branch
free.meaning: WALL THICKNESS of the branch pipe.

free.name: mass_valve
free.meaning: LUMPED MASS of the valve on the branch run.

free.name: mass_connector
free.meaning: LUMPED MASS of the end connector.

free.name: support_connector
free.meaning: TYPE of the far-end support, 'F' (fixed) or 'S' (slotted). A string; only these two are valid.
free.note: 'F' (fixed) or 'S' (slotted), validated live -- ties the branch END to the EA-ST structural node. Per the CSV's own oam_connection_representation field: 'Type recorded (F/S) but no parametric constraint set alongside it yet' -- confirmed by source search, this string is validated and feeds support_code (a display label, e.g. 'L-FT'/'Z-ST') and NOTHING else. No arm, gap, or stiffness value is derived from it, unlike GD-ST/GD-SB's active_connectors(), which returns a full (slot, x, type, arm, gap) tuple per connector.

derived.name: connector_axis
derived.note: Table II / Fig 15 -- HORIZONTAL for L (sliding guide), VERTICAL for Z (rigid to the EA-ST top plate). Drives which edge of a paired GD-ST moves in top_structure_for_branch().

derived.name: support_code
derived.note: the source paper's support-layout code fragment (L-FT-/L-ST-/Z-FT-/Z-ST-). A display label built from support_connector, confirming that field's only real consumer.

derived.name: path
derived.expr: list of (node_suffix, x, y) tuples, Tee to connector
derived.note: L: tee, elbow, valve, end (4 stations). Z: tee, elbow1, valve, elbow2, end (5 stations). y NEGATIVE = rising above the header. The valve IS a real node on this polyline (not a station reported alongside it) specifically so point_masses can attach to it -- see scope.valveNodeIsMandatoryNotPreferred.

derived.name: extent
derived.note: axial footprint the branch SHADOWS on the header -- not owned (owns(x) is always False), just the span reported for bookkeeping/plotting.

derived.name: extent
derived.expr: extent = (centre_x, centre_x + P_b1)  -- ONE-SIDED, not symmetric
derived.meaning: GD-B is the ONLY component whose extent is not centred on centre_x. The Tee sits AT centre_x and the branch runs away from it in +x, so there is no halfExtent: the component starts at its centre_x rather than straddling it. Placing a neighbour to its left means abutting centre_x itself, not centre_x - something. See edas:shared#/chaining.

params.defaultForNote: default_for(pipe, variant) is the SINGLE place the 10D/2D-or-3.5D/2.5D-or-1.25D ratios are computed. NOTE the signature takes a second required-by-convention argument (variant), unlike every other default_for in this corpus (all single-argument, pipe only) -- because P_b2 and P_bc genuinely differ by variant. A caller building this component must supply variant to BOTH the constructor and default_for consistently, or the two will silently disagree; nothing in source enforces that the two match.

junctions: Tee -> pipeline (header structural line), via the base Component.junctions() mechanism
geometry.verifiedLive: L: geometry_nodes()=4 (tee=MANDATORY, elbow=PREFERRED, valve=MANDATORY, end=PREFERRED), geometry_lines()=3, all owns_contact=False. Z: geometry_nodes()=5 (tee=MANDATORY, elbow1=PREFERRED, valve=MANDATORY, elbow2=PREFERRED, end=PREFERRED), geometry_lines()=4, all owns_contact=False. structural_nodes() shares coordinates and priority with geometry_nodes() in both variants -- 'the branch pipe's centreline IS its structural line'. junctions() returns exactly one entry in both variants: (tee_node_id, 'pipeline').
geometry.section: REAL Section throughout every structural line (OD=OD_branch, t=t_branch, owner=code_full) -- unlike edes:GD-ST/edes:GD-SB, whose members use stiffness_ratio because they have no genuine pipe-like cross-section. GD-B is genuine pipe, so its stiffness is mesh-independent, same category as edes:GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP/GD-VLV rather than edes:GD-ST/GD-SB.

constraints.repair: for a Z-branch, set P_b3 strictly between 0 and P_b2
constraints.note: Z-only. Confirmed live at both boundaries (0.0 and P_b2 both rejected).

constraints.repair: set P_bv strictly between 0 and P_b1
constraints.note: STRICT at both ends deliberately -- at 0 or P_b1 the valve node would coincide with an elbow node, giving `path` two entries at one coordinate and a zero-length element. Confirmed live at both boundaries.

constraints.repair: reduce OD_branch below the header's OD_pipe

constraintEquivalence.method: probe vs live validate(), across both variants and invalid variant/support_connector strings

nonConstraints: P_bc is never validated against anything -- it is not read by any method, so no geometric consequence exists for it to be checked against (see scope.p_b3AndP_bcUndocumented)

no check relating P_bc to the actual distance from the Tee to wherever a paired GD-ST's connector slot ends up -- the two are never compared, since P_bc feeds nothing and top_structure_for_branch() computes the real tie-in independently from path[-1]

no upper bound on P_b1/P_b2/P_b3/P_bv magnitude beyond the strict pairwise relations already checked -- geometric validity != evidence coverage, same convention as every other component in this corpus

no check that provenance=DESIGN is appropriate given the fully open designCode status

rows.reason: support_connector='F' (fixed) is a valid, live value -- but per the CSV's own oam_connection_representation field, the type is recorded with NO parametric constraint set alongside it (no arm/gap/stiffness), unlike edes:GD-ST/GD-SB's active_connectors(). dofStatus is provisional rather than confirmed for this reason: no DOF table or force-transfer rule has been written for this connection at all, only a validated label.
support_connector='S' (slotted) -- same gap as F above
support_connector only accepts 'F' or 'S' -- P and D are not valid values for this field, categorical by the source paper's own -FT-/-ST- support taxonomy
same as P above -- not part of the -FT-/-ST- taxonomy this field represents

slots.position: branch root, on the header structural line at centre_x
slots.note: welded, but NOT a chain mate point in the weldL/weldR sense -- it attaches the branch TO the header rather than continuing the header line through it. Realised as a declared junction (junctions() returns exactly one entry, (tee_node_id, 'pipeline')), not as an end-to-end mate with a neighbouring inline component.

NOT a weld at all -- ties to an edes:GD-ST / edes:GD-SB connector slot, typed by support_connector ('F' fixed or 'S' slotted). This is the branch's true AssemblyFeature in the OAM sense, per the FBS/OAM reconciliation CSV ('End connector is the AssemblyFeature -- ties to an EA-ST slot').

assemblyFeatures.whyNotWeldLWeldR: edes:GD-TP, edes:GD-TT, edes:GD-VLV and edes:GD-PIP all carry symmetric welded end stations named weldL/weldR, because each is an INLINE component: the header line enters one end and leaves the other. GD-B is not inline -- it is IW-B, the only branch class, and it LEAVES the header rather than continuing it. Its two ends are therefore asymmetric and differently typed: tee is a welded junction onto the header, end is a bolted/slotted connector onto an external structure. Applying the weldL/weldR convention here would be wrong in both directions -- it would imply the two ends are interchangeable welds, and it would imply the branch continues a line it actually departs from. VERIFIED LIVE 1Sep26: component_spec.BranchPiping emits :tee and :end, not :weldL/:weldR, consistent with this.
assemblyFeatures.strictnessCaveat: whether these are OAMFeatures in NISTIR 7436's strict sense or merely Features depends on whether the component is mated in a given layout -- see edes:shared#/frameworks OAM.usedButLooser.AssemblyFeature candidacy. The tee end is effectively always mated (a branch with no header attachment is not a branch); the end connector is likewise always mated in a complete ILS, but its mate is recorded nowhere on this component -- see required below.
required: a genuine parametric constraint set (arm/gap/stiffness) alongside support_connector, matching what edes:GD-ST/GD-SB provide per slot -- currently just a validated label (see permittedConnections)

GD-B carries no reciprocal reference to the specific GD-ST/GD-SB instance it connects to -- the tie only exists in the direction top_structure_for_branch() builds it (GD-ST built FROM a branch), not as a stored relationship either component holds
assemblyFeatures.featureScopedTypes: candidateTypes differ sharply by feature here, and this component is the clearest case for why the component-level rows are inadequate: tee accepts W only (a weld onto the header), end accepts F or S only (the support_connector taxonomy, which validate() enforces as exactly those two). No feature on this component accepts P or D, yet a component-level reading of the rows would suggest otherwise.

behaviourDerived.mechanism: per the CSV: branch stiffness behaviour varies depending on the support conditions (F vs S) -- not yet quantified, behaviourExpected below is a placeholder per shared.behaviourExpected convention
behaviourDerived.referenceBase: not established -- GD-B never touches the roller/stinger system (contact_at unconditionally None), so no 'plain pipe at same stinger radius' baseline applies the way it does for edes:GD-TP

rollerContact.reason: rises away from the rollers by design -- categorical, same class of fact as edes:GD-ST's inability to own contact, for the identical structural reason (both are entirely off the roller/stinger axis)

behaviourDerived.pointMasses: IMPLEMENTED -- (valve, mass_valve) and (end, mass_connector), both 3000 kg default. Verified live: point_loads(g=9.80665) returns Fy=29419.95 N at each mass node, POSITIVE (y-positive-down convention, so a downward gravity load is positive Fy) -- both the valve and the connector pull the branch down onto whatever supports it. g is an explicit method argument defaulting to config.G, not a constant reached for internally, specifically so a caller running a different acceleration case can supply one without this module having an opinion.

usedInLayouts.note: Back-links to worked layouts containing this component, generated mechanically from the layout library on 1Sep26 -- not hand-written, so they cannot drift from it by authoring error, though they WILL go stale if the library changes and this is not regenerated. Their purpose is placement guidance: this file describes what the component IS and what its own constraints are, but says nothing about where along a header to put one or what to put either side of it. A worked archetype answers that by example. paramsUsed are the archetype's own values verbatim; anchors are published table rows that override them.

ILS-ILT.purpose: Branch piping teed off the header, rising to a support on the top structure. The branch adds a load path that leaves the header, travels through the structure and returns to the pipe at the structure

defects.summary: point_masses() returned the ELBOW node ('elbow' for L, 'elbow2' for Z) as the valve mass location, while its own docstring claimed mid-run placement -- at defaults this put the 3 mT valve mass at x=0.000 (L) or x=4.064 (Z) against a true mid-run of 2.032 m, a full half-run error in the moment arm for a mass on a cantilevered branch
defects.fix: introduced P_bv (Optional, defaulting to P_b1/2 in __post_init__, resolved before validate() runs) as a real node on the `path` polyline, and point_masses() now attaches to that node instead of an elbow

regressionCase.status: none recorded yet -- no Foundation Sec.3 equivalent has been run for GD-B

openQuestions: no Function in the authored set (Func1-5) or the proposed EA-side set (Func6-8) fits GD-B -- Func9 added as the third IW-class Function, per the CSV's own explicit statement that this is 'evidence the Func taxonomy gap is real'; whether Func9 should eventually be split (e.g. an F-support vs S-support distinction) is unexamined

P_bc is stored, validated by nothing, and read by nothing -- either a real consumer needs to be written for it, or it should be marked deprecated/removed rather than left silently unused; currently a caller has no way to discover this without reading source

the branch-to-structure tie (top_structure_for_branch) is one-directional and unrecorded on either component -- GD-B does not know which GD-ST/GD-SB it connects to, and neither stores the relationship after construction; whether this needs to become a real declared reference (analogous to junctions()) once an ILS-level assembly actually needs to walk the connection is open

designCode left fully open -- GD-B is the first EA-adjacent/IW-B component with a REAL section (unlike GD-ST/GD-SB/GD-SH), so it is the closest fit yet to shared.designCode's stated rule, but was not evaluated against it because section_at(x) answers 'no interface at this header x' before the rule's pipe-shaped-vs-non-pipe-interface distinction is ever reached -- whether the rule should be restated to also cover a component's OWN section (not just the header's) is unexamined

P_b3's placeholder default (P_b2/2) has no basis in the source paper at all, per source's own comment -- unlike GD-B's other undocumented default (P_bv), which at least has an intuitive 'mid-run' justification, P_b3's half-rise placeholder is acknowledged in source as arbitrary
